facts.text: focusKey returns the element's tag name joined with its data-target by a pipe, so a rebuilt control with the same target is found again.
When data-target is absent focusKey falls back to href, giving links a comparable identity across a quiet rebuild.
focusKey reads data-target first and only then looks at href, so a control's target wins over any href it carries.
findByKey walks each child depth-first and returns the first descendant whose focusKey equals the requested key, or null.
renderPanel takes its focus source from doc.activeElement only when quiet is set and that element sits inside the panel.
Every renderPanel begins by clearing the panel, unhiding it, and adding a Close button with id g-close.
The fact panel heading is the word Fact followed by cap(fd.id, 64).
For a subject node the facts row shows String(Number(sd.facts) || 0), so a missing or bad count renders as 0.
A subject whose boundary flag is set gets a boundary row reading a fact of this subject refers into the graph.
at: a fact of this subject refers into the graph

facts.text: The fact panel shows subject, kind, status and confidence rows, each value passed through cap with its own limit.
Tags in the fact panel are each capped at 40 and joined with a comma and space, or shown as none when empty.
The fact text is rendered in a pre element capped at 2000 characters.
Refs listed in fd.unresolved are added to the Refs out list and each one is marked (external).
A quiet renderPanel restores focus only for a reader already in the panel, targeting the matching rebuilt control via findByKey or the heading.
A non-quiet renderPanel focuses the heading and then calls resize and schedule.
Referenced-by lists come from refList with outgoing false, and an empty list gets one item reading none.
A subject panel adds Open subject and Graph from here links, separated by a pipe, both built through hashLink.
A fact panel adds an Open fact link built by hashLink and a section headed Refs out.
The panel heading gets tabindex -1 so the code can place focus on it after a rebuild.
closePanel is bound as the click handler of the Close button that renderPanel creates.
closePanel sets selected to null, hides the panel, clears its text, then calls resize and schedule.
hit converts the pointer to world coordinates and searches nodes from the last so the topmost one wins, using radius plus 3 divided by view.scale.
expand derives the subject from the node id for subjects or from data.subject for facts, and returns early unless ID_RE accepts it.
expand sets the status text to the loading marker while its fetch is outstanding, then clears it on success.
A failed expand writes cap(err.message, 200) to the status line prefixed with error:.
expand restarts the layout with 20 ticks when merge added nodes, otherwise releases holds if no layout is pending.
After a merge expand records the fetched subject with remember so later refreshes include it.
Before merging an expansion expand marks every existing node as held so their positions survive.
at: for (var k = 0; k < nodes.length; k++) nodes[k].hold = true;

facts.text: endDrag opens the panel for the pressed node only when the accumulated movement is at most 4 pixels.
endDrag releases the pointer capture only when the canvas still holds it, and sets the cursor back to grab.
onKey ignores any key event carrying ctrlKey, metaKey or altKey, so browser and OS shortcuts are left alone.
Keys typed into INPUT, TEXTAREA, SELECT or editable content never reach the graph shortcuts.
From a button or link onKey acts only on Escape, which closes the panel.
Pressing f or F fits the graph to the stage and schedules a redraw.
Pressing Enter, e or E expands the node that is currently selected, when one is.
url builds the graph request as /api/graph with the subject URL-encoded plus depth, facts and max_nodes values.
pump returns at once and sets dirty when a refresh is already running, so only one request is in flight.
pump applies removals from every queued delta row before it classifies any of them.
When dirty, pendingFull or pendingRows remain at the end, pump clears dirty and calls itself again.
at: if (dirty || pendingFull || pendingRows.length) { dirty = false; return pump(); }

facts.text: pump passes finish as both the success and the failure handler of the fetch chain.
A queued row that pump did not handle as a removal is passed to restore so a live row can lift it.
pump stops classifying rows at the first row that asks for a full refresh.
A full refresh refetches the root and every subject in the expanded set.
A subject fetch that fails is swallowed so one missing subject does not abort the rest of the refresh.
at: that subject is gone: keep the nodes we have and go on

facts.text: finish clears refreshing before it tests destroyed, so the refresh gate reopens on every path.
finish treats a refresh that recovered the initial load as a first layout, clearing the error and then resizing and fitting.
Nodes added by a delta flush receive GLOW_FRAMES of glow so each one flashes once.
at: for (var a = 0; a < added.length; a++) added[a].glow = GLOW_FRAMES;

facts.text: finish leaves holds in place while a layout is still pending, because the settle releases them.
at: its last tick releases every hold

facts.text: pump refuses to run once the view is destroyed or live updates have stopped.
applyRemoval treats a facts row as a removal when its op is delete or its fact_status is retracted.
applyRemoval records the removed key with the row's seq, or -1 when that seq is not finite.
applyRemoval builds a key only when the row carries a string fact_id or subject_id.
restore clears a removed key only when the row's seq is finite and greater than the seq that removed it.
restore returns immediately for a row whose op is delete.
classify asks for a full refresh for any row touching the subjects table or naming no subject_id.
at: if (row.tbl === 'subjects' || row.subject_id === null || row.subject_id === undefined) return { full: true };

facts.text: A refs row whose subject is not on screen makes classify refetch the root, since it may add an inbound edge.
applyFrame drops every change whose seq is not finite or is at or below lastSeen, treating it as a redelivery.
After the rows, applyFrame raises lastSeen to the frame's to value, or else to its next value.
applyFrame passes the rows it accepted to the activity feed with feed.ingest.
pointerdown records the hit node, the pointer position, a zero movement counter and the pointerId in drag, then captures the pointer.
at: drag = { node: nd, x: p[0], y: p[1], moved: 0, id: ev.pointerId };

facts.text: pointermove adds the absolute horizontal and vertical change to drag.moved before applying the delta to the node or the view.
Dragging a node beyond 4 pixels pins it and raises alpha to at least 0.3 unless motion is reduced.
Dragging empty space pans the view by adding the pointer delta to view.tx and view.ty.
The wheel handler zooms by exp of minus deltaY times 0.0015 and clamps the scale between 0.02 and 8.
The wheel handler keeps the point under the cursor fixed by adjusting the view translation before setting the scale.
A double click on a node found by hit calls expand for that node.
stopStream clears its stored stream, detaches onerror, and calls close when the object provides one.
stopStream returns at once when no stream is stored.
stopLive sets liveStopped, stops the stream, clears both timers, and discards pending rows and flags.
scheduleFlush replaces any pending flush timer with a new timeout of DEBOUNCE_MS that calls pump.
refillFeed resets the feed and reloads its history from /api/changes?last=50.
refillFeed ingests the fetched changes only when the body carries a changes array and a feed still exists.
afterReset applies removals for rows still queued for the debounce before it calls refresh.
at: for (var k = 0; k < queued.length; k++) applyRemoval(queued[k]);

facts.text: afterReset sets lastSeen to the reset number when it is finite, before refilling the feed and refreshing.
onChanges treats a frame whose reset member is set as a discontinuity and routes it to onReset.
onChanges returns without a frame when parsing ev.data as JSON throws.
onResetEvent parses the event data as an integer and falls back to lastSeen when that is not finite.
pollChanges returns early while pollBusy is set, and pollPage clears that flag on both success and failure.
pollPage requests /api/changes with since and limit once lastSeen is non-negative, and with last and limit before that.
When a page reports truncated, pollPage fetches the next page immediately while page plus one stays below POLL_PAGES.
pollPage sends every page through applyFrame and then schedules a flush.
startPolling stops any stream and installs a poll timer that calls pollChanges every POLL_MS.
startPolling returns without action when a poll timer is already installed.
listen falls back to startPolling when the window provides no EventSource constructor.
listen opens /api/events and appends a since query value when lastSeen is non-negative.
The stream's onerror starts polling when the EventSource readyState is 2, the closed state.
listen registers onChanges for changes events and onResetEvent for reset events.
listen is called after initialLoad even when that load failed, so refresh still works.
initialLoad fetches the graph for rootId, merges the payload, refreshes the header and resizes the stage.
With reduced motion initialLoad settles the layout with tick calls, fits, and draws once.
With motion allowed initialLoad runs 60 layout ticks before fitting and scheduling the animation loop.
destroy removes the keydown and resize listeners that mount added to the document and window.
destroy cancels a pending animation frame when rafHandle holds one.
destroy calls feed.destroy and clears the feed reference when a feed was mounted.
The mount result exposes lastSeen through a getter described as read-only for tests and diagnostics.
The feed history is requested only when a feed is mounted, otherwise history resolves immediately.
The revision baseline is fetched only when EventSource or setInterval exists on the window.
The returned merge wrapper substitutes null for a missing anchorKey, refreshes the header and returns the added nodes.
at: merge: function (payload, anchorKey) { var added = merge(payload, anchorKey || null); refreshHeader(); return added; },

facts.text: The module assigns DossierGraph, holding mount and ID_RE, onto window.
Clicking the Fit button calls fit and then schedule.
The returned object exposes expand and refresh so the page can drive the mounted view.
local turns a pointer event into canvas coordinates by subtracting the canvas rectangle's left and top from clientX and clientY.
showPanel stores the node as selected and renders the panel in non-quiet mode.
